verdicts.label: quality_relevant
verdicts.justification: Scores whether the comment supplies new evidence (measurements, records, surveys, field observations) into the record, which is a core substantive-merit dimension of regulatory input.

verdicts.label: quality_relevant
verdicts.justification: Requires quoting/citing the ambiguous term, laying out competing readings, and stating the divergent practical consequence -- genuine analytical engagement with the regulatory text, not a surface marker.

verdicts.label: quality_relevant
verdicts.justification: Scores whether a reasoned failure-mechanism is given for why the rule will not achieve its aim; explicitly instructs judging the reasoning, not tone or confidence.

verdicts.label: incidental
verdicts.justification: Scores the mere absence of external citation/data (anecdote-only sourcing), which a substance-free comment ('I don't like this, it hurt my business') can score high on; it flags evidentiary TYPE/shape rather than any analytical contribution, unlike P10 which requires generalization.

verdicts.label: incidental
verdicts.justification: Instruction explicitly states this is 'a disclosure feature of the text: score its presence, not whether the relationship lends authority' -- a submitter-identity fingerprint, not merit.

verdicts.label: incidental
verdicts.justification: Scores a self-presented identity claim (speaking for many parties) as it appears in the text with 'no outside verification expected' -- a submitter-identity/packaging fingerprint, not the substance of any argument made.

verdicts.label: quality_relevant
verdicts.justification: Scores whether the comment proposes concrete monitoring/verification mechanisms (indicators, data collection, reporting, revisit triggers) -- substantive engagement with implementation and accountability.

verdicts.label: quality_relevant
verdicts.justification: Scores whether the comment names specific populations/firms/places bearing differentiated costs or benefits and explains the inequality -- substantive distributional analysis.

verdicts.label: incidental
verdicts.justification: Framed as 'fluency' scored by whether citations appear 'in the register a regulatory practitioner uses' -- this instructs judging professional-drafting style/register rather than whether any claim or revision is substantively correct or useful (contrast with P16/P17, which require correctness or a concrete ask).

verdicts.label: quality_relevant
verdicts.justification: Requires the firsthand account to be reported concretely AND translated into a rule-relevant general pattern beyond the writer's own case -- an analytical contribution, not mere anecdote.

verdicts.label: incidental
verdicts.justification: Instruction explicitly states this is 'a surface feature of the document: score how much residue is present, nothing else' (portal headers, OCR errors, filenames).

verdicts.label: quality_relevant
verdicts.justification: Scores concrete specification of implementation mechanics (forms, offices, transition steps, testing scenarios, timelines, documentation) -- substantive operational content.

verdicts.label: incidental
verdicts.justification: Instruction explicitly states this is a 'surface feature of format: score only the salutation and signature block' -- letter furniture, not content.

verdicts.label: incidental
verdicts.justification: Instruction explicitly states this is 'a self-presentation feature of the text: score how prominent the display is, not whether the credentials are impressive.'

verdicts.label: quality_relevant
verdicts.justification: Scores whether a specific procedural request is made with a reason grounded in the record or the requester's circumstances -- an actionable, reasoned regulatory input.

verdicts.label: quality_relevant
verdicts.justification: Requires the legal connection to be stated correctly ('states that connection correctly as far as the text shows'), so accuracy of legal reasoning is judged, not merely the presence of legal language.

verdicts.label: quality_relevant
verdicts.justification: Requires an exact provision cited AND a specific revision stated -- concrete, actionable engagement with the rule text.

verdicts.label: quality_relevant
verdicts.justification: Scores precision of the requested change (exact replacement language, numeric thresholds, definitions) as opposed to bare support/opposition -- substantive actionability.

verdicts.label: quality_relevant
verdicts.justification: Scores whether a specific, actionable gap in the proposal is identified (an unaddressed scenario, unassigned responsibility, etc.) with what filling it would take -- substantive critique of the proposal's completeness.

verdicts.label: incidental
verdicts.justification: Instruction explicitly states this is 'a surface feature: do not consider what the number is used for or whether it is correct' -- bare presence of digits.

verdicts.label: incidental
verdicts.justification: Instruction explicitly states this is 'a surface feature of the wording, scored as such and not as a judgment of quality' -- template/boilerplate similarity.

verdicts.label: quality_relevant
verdicts.justification: Scores whether the comment distinguishes strong from weak evidence, names assumptions/limitations, and calibrates confidence -- substantive epistemic rigor.

verdicts.label: quality_relevant
verdicts.justification: Scores whether a concrete, implementable alternative is proposed and its fit to the rule's legitimate objective explained -- substantive constructive engagement.

verdicts.label: quality_relevant
verdicts.justification: Scores whether a step-by-step causal chain (including behavioral response) from rule to effect is traced -- substantive reasoning about mechanism, not just asserted harm/benefit.

verdicts.label: quality_relevant
verdicts.justification: Scores whether the comment identifies responsible actors, workflows, dependencies, and failure modes bearing on whether the rule can work in practice -- substantive implementation analysis.
